lines.text: Game night. Your friends, your dice, and a game master who never cancels.
Open Hearthmaster on a laptop, put the table on your TV, and press start.
One shared microphone hears the whole table. Say your name once, and it knows every voice.
Every hero and monster stands on the board as a hand-painted miniature.
Walls block sight. Doors open. And the fog lifts only where your heroes can see.
I throw open the storeroom door!
As the storeroom door swings wide, two skeletal figures jerk upright.
In combat it rolls initiative, runs every turn, and throws real physics dice, with cover, spell slots and hit points all tracked.
Victories, defeats and last stands each get their moment.
Fallen foes drop loot you can walk over and pick up.
Every player's sheet lives on their phone, with a map of where they stand.
Split the party? Each group keeps its own scene, and the TV cuts between them.
Every character speaks in their own voice...
I won't forget this, Sister. You've earned a friend in the harbor.
...and remembers how you treated them.
Short a player? Pull up an AI companion.
Pip, Brienne's looking to you for a keen-eyed take on that wreck.
Honestly, the glare off the water beat my eyes today, so I couldn't make out much.
It plays its own hero, in its own voice.
And your heroes carry over, from one campaign to the next.
Hearthmaster. A game master for your kitchen table.
Gather your party.
